value.title: SMASH: Co-designing Software Compression and Hardware-Accelerated Indexing for Efficient Sparse Matrix Operations

value.statement: A set Bitmap-0 bit represents a nonzero block of fixed compression-ratio size in the contiguous NZA. A higher-level set bit represents a lower bitmap region with at least one set bit. Only nonzero blocks of lower bitmaps are stored; NZA blocks are appended in format order.
limitations: Paper specification only. Actual BMU/ISA, bit encoding, address translation and physical-memory identities remain unbound.

value.statement: Increasing block compression can retain zero elements inside represented NZA blocks. An indexed nonzero block therefore does not establish individual lane nonzero validity.
limitations: Paper specification only. Actual BMU/ISA, bit encoding, address translation and physical-memory identities remain unbound.

value.statement: BMU groups each dedicate bitmap SRAM buffers, configuration state and row/column output registers to one matrix. The examined implementation uses256-byte buffers and constrains bitmap compression to fit buffer traversal.
limitations: Paper specification only. Actual BMU/ISA, bit encoding, address translation and physical-memory identities remain unbound.

value.statement: BMU traverses hierarchical set bits depth first, retaining each level index. Compression ratios combine those indices into the original matrix flat block index; division/modulo by matrix columns gives its row/column.
limitations: Paper specification only. Actual BMU/ISA, bit encoding, address translation and physical-memory identities remain unbound.

value.statement: MATINFO sets dimensions/group; BMAPINFO sets per-level compression/group; RDBMAP fills a selected bitmap buffer from memory; PBMAP scans and updates next block row/column; RDIND copies current row/column to two destination registers.
limitations: Paper specification only. Actual BMU/ISA, bit encoding, address translation and physical-memory identities remain unbound.

value.statement: CPU consumer software iterates block rank and elements to address NZA and performs operand loads and arithmetic. SpMM compares separate matrix block indices before inner-product work. BMU index production alone does not execute those loads or arithmetic.
limitations: Paper specification only. Actual BMU/ISA, bit encoding, address translation and physical-memory identities remain unbound.

value.description: Software hierarchical compression with group-scoped BMU indexing and CPU consumer; no inherited operand-load or arithmetic capability.

value.name: SMASH MICRO2019 bitmap block-index assistance
value.summary: Group-scoped hierarchical bitmap indexing returns matrix coordinates for represented NZA blocks; CPU still performs data loads and numerical operations.

interface.software_supplies: Matrix dimensions, per-level compression ratios and compact bitmaps/NZA, group selection, bitmap buffer loads and consumer block-rank state.
interface.invocation: MATINFO/BMAPINFO configure; RDBMAP loads selected bitmaps; PBMAP advances scanner; RDIND reads current row/column.
interface.outputs: Matrix coordinates of represented blocks. NZA rank and per-element arithmetic/load addressing remain CPU consumer responsibilities.

realization.description: Load/configure group-scoped compressed bitmap hierarchy, depth-first scan a next represented block, retrieve its original matrix row/column and maintain consumer NZA rank separately.

result.form: Two block-coordinate register outputs; no loaded matrix payload or scalar arithmetic result.
result.validity: Only explicitly configured SMASH matrix encoding with correct dimensions/compression/group state and consumer NZA rank.

ordering.scope: One group and declared bitmap traversal
ordering.description: Depth-first set-bit traversal establishes original block coordinates; consumer block rank follows format order. No universal physical request or scalar FP order is implied.

completion.event: PBMAP updates current row/column and RDIND retrieves them.
completion.visibility: Index availability is not operand-read, arithmetic, writeback or host-visible kernel completion. Hardware EOF/fault signaling is not specified by this operation record.

type_constraints.notes: BMU returns coordinates; concrete coordinate/register bit widths and matrix payload transport datatype are not proved by inspected sections.

operations.datatype_notes: No matrix FP/integer type, per-lane nonzero predicate or arithmetic ABI is inferred.
limitations: Block can contain zero lanes; exact per-lane validity unavailable from bitmap alone.
No generic gather, returned operand payload or ordered reduction capability.

requirements.description: Prove per-level compression, nonzero child block storage order, bit ordering, matrix extent and snapshot integrity; declared parent bits must match lower bitmap blocks.
Bind each represented block to its format rank and complete NZA extent; do not mistake a block-present bit for all lanes nonzero.
Bind configuration and RDBMAP/PBMAP/RDIND to the same selected matrix/group generation. Group0 is valid only when actually selected, never a missing-owner default.
Prove actual ratio units and per-level encoded byte footprints fit selected BMU buffers. A semantic decoded bitmap is not a physical transport admission proof.
Prove original consumer block/element bounds, edge padding and matrix indexing independently; BMU coordinates do not certify arithmetic or load correctness.
Authenticate BMU/ISA source, coordinate width, transport endianness, fault/EOF behavior, ownership, translation/protection and kernel completion.

parameters.notes: Examined implementation reference; not NZA payload capacity.
Paper256-byte bitmap/2048:1 reference. Actual level units and byte footprints must be bound; helper semantic acceptance cannot substitute.
Paper supports multiple independent matrix groups; universal count/selector ABI not inferred from examples.

internal_mechanisms.description: Per-group SRAM holds one bitmap block at a time; configuration and output registers belong to the selected matrix group.
Set-bit traversal descends represented child blocks and combines retained level indices into a block coordinate.
Dimension/ratio/group state and saved traversal indices establish block coordinates; consumer NZA rank tracks contiguous block order.
RDIND reads current coordinate outputs after PBMAP. CPU loads and computes separately.

limitations: Abstract canonical bitmap contract is not BMU RTL, an executable SMASH ISA or measured hardware.
Partial logical NZA blocks need an explicit edge-padding contract; helper rejects them rather than inventing padding.
Concrete bit packing/endianness, register widths, faults and EOF transport unspecified.
No generic graph traversal, gather, arithmetic or original benchmark correctness is granted.
